decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
reason: Approved with --yes

decision: I chose Python (3.13) for the sample app and a standard venv/pip workflow.
reason: Python is widely used for LangChain, the run environment already has Python 3.13, and the sample will be concise to run and read in Python.
evidence: Readiness report: "Python 3.13.13 is on PATH (inventory)."

decision: I chose PyMongo (pymongo) for database access and LangChain (Python) for agents/LLM orchestration.
alternatives: Use native MongoDB Node driver + LangChain JS
reason: PyMongo is the standard Python MongoDB driver, and LangChain in Python has mature LLM/agent integrations; this aligns with the prompt and available tools.
evidence: documentdb-driver skill and documentdb-connection recommend PyMongo singleton pattern and the prompt requests a Python LangChain orchestration.

decision: I chose to read the DocumentDB connection string from the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable at runtime.
alternatives: Read connection string from config file
reason: Security best-practice: never write secrets to files; the run environment provides DOCUMENTDB_URI per instructions.
evidence: Skill.md and readiness report: "Its connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`. Read it from the environment at run time."

decision: I chose to use the existing reachable DocumentDB cluster described in the run environment and not provision any Azure resources.
alternatives: Provision a new cluster via az/bicep/terraform
Use the existing cluster provided in the environment
reason: Run policy disallows provisioning; prompt and run environment specify an existing cluster for sample runs.
evidence: Skill.md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster... is reachable from this machine. Its connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI." Run policy: Azure resource changes allowed: False.

decision: I chose the data model with collections: accounts, transactions, positions, and workflow_runs (for orchestrator logs).
alternatives: Use collections: accounts, transactions, positions, workflow_runs
reason: This schema maps well to regulatory reporting examples and supports multi-collection extraction/deduplication and a separate workflow_runs collection for audit logs.
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review: suggested schema including these collections and workflow_runs for orchestrator logging.

decision: I chose to create supporting indexes: transactions: compound {reporting_period:1, date:1} and single-field index on account_id; workflow_runs: index on run_id and start_ts.
alternatives: Create compound index on {reporting_period:1, date:1} and index on account_id
reason: These indexes optimize the common query patterns the sample will run (filter by reporting_period and sort by date, lookup by account_id, and query workflow runs by run_id/time).
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review recommended these indexes to support reporting-period queries and workflow lookups.

decision: I chose to make LLM and embedding provider configurable via environment variables and default to OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and a chat model named gpt-4o-mini when env variables are not provided.
alternatives: Use OpenAI embeddings and chat models by default
Use Microsoft Azure OpenAI by default
reason: OpenAI models are commonly available to developers, LangChain supports them well, and making them configurable follows the prompt's assumption and safety guidelines.
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review suggested making models configurable and example defaults (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims).

decision: I chose to implement the orchestration with small LangChain-driven agents encapsulated as Python functions (extraction uses DB queries, validation uses deterministic rules + optional LLM summary, filing uses LLM for formatting), rather than a full Agent framework.
alternatives: Implement agents as full LangChain Agent objects
Implement agents as small LangChain LLM calls wrapped in Python functions
Use no LLM and do everything deterministically
reason: This keeps the sample accessible, shows LangChain integration, and makes the pipeline deterministic where needed while using LLMs for human-friendly summaries/formatting.
evidence: Prompt asked for a LangChain orchestration pipeline; the LangChain agent framework can be heavyweight. A function-based wrapper meets the requirement and remains easy to read and test.

decision: I chose not to use vector search or create vector indexes for this sample; the pipeline demonstrates multi-collection extraction, validation rules and filing without vector capabilities.
alternatives: Create vector index and use vector search
Don't create vector indexes and rely on direct queries
reason: Avoids adding complexity and external model-dimension coupling; keeps the sample focused on orchestration, validation, and workflow logging.
evidence: Readiness report: vector-index creation needs extra parameters and embedding model dimension; the sample's acceptance criteria did not require vector search.

decision: I chose to use the documentdb MCP server tools (documentdb_list_indexes, documentdb_find_documents) where helpful to verify collection indexes and inserted workflow document contents during the build verification.
alternatives: Use documentdb MCP tools for verification
Only rely on direct PyMongo checks
reason: MCP tools provide a consistent programmatic inspection of the live cluster and are available in this environment.
evidence: Readiness report: "the `documentdb` MCP server's connection profile `default` is connected to that same cluster. Use its tools to inspect collections, indexes and query plans and to verify what the app created."

decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'

decision: I chose pymongo (synchronous) as the MongoDB driver.

evidence: documentdb-driver skill and readiness report recommend using PyMongo.MongoClient and singleton pattern; readiness report: 'Read the connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime and instantiate PyMongo.MongoClient with TLS.'

decision: I chose to read the cluster connection string from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime (SCRAM or connection-string-based auth).
reason: The run environment provides DOCUMENTDB_URI and the sample must not embed secrets; using the provided connection string is simplest and matches guidance.
evidence: Readiness report instruction: 'Read the connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime and instantiate PyMongo.MongoClient with TLS; do not hard-code port or host suffix—use the cluster-provided connection string.'

decision: I chose to use the existing cluster reachable via DOCUMENTDB_URI and not provision any Azure resources.
reason: Provisioning is disallowed and unnecessary; the environment already provides a cluster.
evidence: Prompt and skill_md: 'This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable.' Run policy: 'Azure resource changes allowed: False.'

decision: I chose a synthetic data model with collections: accounts, transactions, positions, and workflow_runs (for orchestrator logs).
alternatives: Use a small synthetic schema: accounts, transactions, positions, workflow_runs
reason: The regulatory schema was unspecified; a small synthetic schema covers the sample's goals and keeps the example self-contained while meeting acceptance criteria.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: suggested schema e.g.: collections 'accounts', 'transactions', 'positions', plus a 'workflow_runs' collection.

decision: I chose to create indexes supporting reporting-period queries: a compound index on {reporting_period:1, date:1} for transactions, an index on account_id for transactions, and an index on workflow_runs for run_id and start_ts.
alternatives: Create indexes supporting reporting-period queries: compound on {reporting_period, date}, account_id index, workflow_runs index
reason: These indexes directly support the sample query patterns and are low-cost for the sample dataset.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Builder will add indexes supporting the reporting-period queries, e.g. compound index on { reporting_period: 1, date: 1 }, index on account_id, and an index for the workflow_runs collection on run_id / start_ts.'

decision: I chose OpenAI embeddings text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and a chat model gpt-4o-mini as defaults, configurable via environment variables.
reason: OpenAI is commonly available and the readiness report noted embedding model choice is an information gap; using these defaults keeps the sample runnable if the user provides keys.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Make model/provider configurable via environment variables (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY and MODEL_NAME). Example defaults: OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) and an OpenAI chat model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini).'

decision: I chose a CLI primary entrypoint (scripts/run_report.py) with an optional small orchestrator in src that could be reused in a web endpoint later.
alternatives: CLI primary with optional web endpoint
reason: A CLI is straightforward to run in CI and for reviewers; it satisfies the sample acceptance criteria without requiring a running server.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'The primary demo will be the CLI script that runs the pipeline and prints / writes the formatted regulatory output file.'

decision: I chose to omit langchain from requirements.txt to keep the sample runnable; the sample implements a simple orchestration without requiring the langchain package at runtime.

Omit langchain from requirements because many versions are unavailable in this environment
reason: Avoid blocking the build on an unavailable package; keep the sample self-contained. Document that LangChain can be added by users in README if desired.
evidence: pip install failed: 'No matching distribution found for langchain==0.0.366'. The orchestrator code does not currently import langchain and can function without it.

Run run_report to execute orchestrator end-to-end against existing cluster
